# Claritish Introduction {#claritish}
<!-- Agent summary: Claritish = English plus Ageben drop-ins, each spelled as in Ageben. Placement: where English puts an adverb or a short tag such as *you know*; a drop-in applies to the whole clause it sits in. Example: `thomam` *could be*. In your own writing, no italics or quotes; the pages use code font only to show them. -->

**Claritish** is English with a few Ageben words dropped in, called **drop-ins**. Each drop-in says something English has no word for, such as how sure you are, how you know, or what a thank-you was for. You keep speaking English and add the drop-in where English would put an adverb or a short tag such as *you know*.

> The package arrives Friday `thomam`.

`thomam` means *could be*. It applies to the whole clause it sits in, so the sentence says that the package might arrive Friday, and nothing more.

This helps you get a feel for how Ageben influences your thinking. Everything you learn in Claritish is exactly the same in Ageben so this also provides a smoother on-ramp into the full language.

## The lessons {#lessons}
<!-- Agent summary: eleven lessons in a fixed order, each with a few examples and a practice set; later lessons reuse earlier ones, so read them in order the first time. -->

Each lesson is short, with a few examples and a practice set. Some lessons reuse ideas from earlier ones, so read them in order the first time.

- [How sure are you?](could-be.md): one word for *could be*, and what you plan to do about the guess.
- [How do you know?](how-you-know.md): whether a claim was seen, remembered, worked out, or heard.
- [Labels](labels.md): how far a label like *liar* reaches.
- [Can and can't](can-and-cant.md): whether *I can't* means not now, not yet, or never.
- [Thanks and sorry](thanks-and-sorry.md): the sake a thank-you or an apology is about, meaning the need it met or harmed.
- [Allowed and required](allowed-required-agreed.md): who said yes, who demanded it, and whether the person it affects agreed.
- [Oughts and motives](oughts-and-motives.md): the sake a *should* appeals to, and the sake behind what you did.
- [Wants and plans](wants-and-plans.md): a wish you owe no one, and how far a plan is worked out.
- [Decisions and tries](decisions-and-tries.md): how settled a decision is, and a try that is only a trial.
- [What a feeling wants](what-a-feeling-wants.md): the sake behind a feeling, and its urge, meaning what it makes you want to do.
- [Feelings in full](feelings.md): six more urges, whether a feeling will pass, and a fear of what has not happened.

Five pages follow the lessons:

| Page | What it gives you |
|------|-------------------|
| [Bonus: tone marks](tone-marks.md) | seven marks that say how you mean a sentence |
| [Learn the full language](learn.md) | the drop-ins inside a full Ageben sentence, and where to start learning Ageben |

| [Flashcards](flashcards.md) | every drop-in as an Anki flashcard, one deck per lesson |
